findings.evidence: “Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup” names explicit setup but does not distinguish it from running an already configured review or execution, or surface stale-provider diagnosis as a trigger.
findings.fix: Use when the owner wants to set up or refresh ai-kit’s cross-AI review or execute lanes, choose which installed AI CLIs and models to use and in what fallback order, check lane availability or stale OpenCode providers, or ask about an old review-spec.toml migration. Also use when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers offers setup because no lanes exist. Propose separate review and execute sets, confirm effort and opt-ins, then write [lanes] in .aikit/config.toml by default. Announce the exact path and ask before replacing any roster. --check-only reports without persisting changes; --local and --global select the target, not replacement consent. Not for running a review or execution with configured lanes, or editing unrelated config tables.

findings.evidence: “This skill is a Process … executed with Tool-level rigor” describes the artifact’s pattern rather than teaching ai-kit behavior; the rule immediately after it is the useful part.
findings.fix: Keep the factory-subcommand rule and why hand-typed IDs or TOML fail at dispatch. Record the removal of the pattern self-description as redundant.

findings.evidence: The “## NEVER” section contains Steps 1–4 as subordinate headings. The Step 2 routing table indexes questions, but there is no equivalent checkpoint list for the overall process.
findings.fix: Keep the NEVER list as a standalone section and put Steps 0–4 under a workflow heading. Add a short checklist keyed to completed decisions: target and replacement consent, selected sets and probe consent, rendered roster verification, and trust disposition.

findings.evidence: The 479-line body is 6,865 words. It loads both the Codex “BARE model id” walkthrough and the Cursor bracket-ID recipe even for check-only, headless, or session-default-only runs.
findings.fix: Keep the pair-versus-command decision in Step 2.4. Move the complete Codex and Cursor examples, including the bare-ID evidence and listing fallback, into a focused references/runtime-knobs.md and explicitly load only the selected runtime’s section from Step 2.4.

findings.evidence: “Then ask policy.mode (single or double)” presents a mandatory choice without identifying the writer’s built-in single-mode default or preserving the current mode by default on refresh.
findings.fix: Default to the existing mode when refreshing, or single on first setup. Offer double explicitly for an independent second reviewer; leave the other validated choices and consent gates unchanged.

findings.evidence: “--global forces … directly” and “--local also forces local directly” do not specify what to do when both flags are present, although the choice controls which roster can be replaced.
findings.fix: Reject conflicting scope flags before any scope-dependent action; require the owner to select exactly one target before continuing.

findings.evidence: “If the proposal shows an alias group” lets the router-alias assertion pass when the wizard omits the alias entirely. The supplied lane snippet alone does not force a proposal containing that alias.
findings.fix: Stage a deterministic catalog and runtime fixture that returns the supplied alias. Require the named alias to appear in the assumed group, assert that it has no rank or score, and keep the assertion that no heuristic confirmation is asked.

findings.evidence: “Write my reviewer config to the global review-spec file” is labeled positive without clarifying whether this means migrating a legacy roster or writing the retired format. The set has few realistic requests for execute-only setup phrased without lane terminology.
findings.fix: Make the global positive request [lanes] in the user-level config.toml; retain the separate migration positive. Replace an easy negative with a near-miss asking to run an existing execute roster, and add a positive asking which installed coding agent should implement changes and which should take over when it hits quota.

findings.evidence: “Do not run fetch-model-catalog” correctly protects a pending roster outside the approved target, but the next path still needs the catalog: wizard-flow.md step 2 can reload cli-model-selection.md item 3, which runs the same migrating command on the same full snapshot, and Step 3 requires a readable catalog path.
findings.fix: Carry a no-migration decision into Step 2 and any retry. Use a catalog path built or reused without a roster-migrating read; if no such path is available, stop before writing and explain the blocker. Do not re-enter the normal fetch through candidate research or an empty-catalog retry.

findings.evidence: “If any entries exist” follows the raw target read, so a default local check with no local roster can skip the quota section even when the merged view has global lanes. The reverse can occur when --global is passed and only local lanes exist.
findings.fix: Always enumerate effective probe keys with the non-migrating resolver, even when the requested layer’s raw roster is empty. Run the consent gate on those keys, and distinguish an empty effective probe set from a roster inherited from the other layer.

findings.evidence: “When an old roster is pending in either place, say so before running it” permits trust-local --show to migrate an unapproved global roster after a local write. The merged preview calls cfg_combine with migration enabled; notification alone does not authorize that separate change.
findings.fix: Guard both trust forms against migrating a roster outside the approved target. Use a non-migrating preview and trust path if available; otherwise stop at written but untrusted until the owner separately authorizes the affected migration, including backup handling.

findings.evidence: “For any entry without its own line, show its command text from the file” fails for a local execute entry that inherits a command from the user layer and shares a key with a review entry. The flattened preview can omit the execute entry, and the local entry has no command text to show.
findings.fix: Require a role-qualified effective argv for each command-bearing entry, including inherited templates with local substitutions. If the existing preview cannot resolve one, leave the roster untrusted and report the unresolved role and key instead of asking for consent.

findings.evidence: “Ask each named lane’s effort again from the levels the line names” fails for the documented cannot-be-passed refusal: lane_effort.py emits the rejected level and reason, but no replacement levels.
findings.fix: For an out-of-list refusal, re-offer the allowed values plus no effort. For a cannot-be-passed refusal, derive allowed values from the same catalog and runtime evidence or offer no effort if none remain. Clear effort_source whenever its accepted level is removed or changed.

findings.evidence: “codex has no models/list-models subcommand (confirmed via codex --help)” is stated as a standing vendor CLI fact. It neither asks the agent to check that absence on the installed binary nor gives a dated source for the historical observation.
findings.fix: Base model selection on the detected snapshot, and keep the existing missing-list fallback. If the top-level subcommand detail is needed for troubleshooting, tell the agent to check the installed codex --help live or cite the official versioned source and date checked.
